title: RBI FD Rule Changes: Impact on Your Interest Rates
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed banks to offer differential interest rates on bulk deposits. This differentiation can be based on a bank's liquidi.

faq.a: A bulk deposit in India is generally defined as a fixed deposit with an amount of ₹2 crores or more. These are typically placed by corporates, institutions, or high-net-worth individuals.

faq.q: Does this rule directly change my small FD rates?
faq.a: No, this rule primarily applies to bulk deposits (₹2 crores and above). It does not directly mandate or facilitate changes to interest rates on smaller, retail fixed deposits.

faq.q: What is the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)?
faq.a: The LCR is a regulatory requirement for banks to hold sufficient high-quality liquid assets to cover their net cash outflows over a 30-day stress period, ensuring they can meet short-term obligations.

faq.q: Should I move my FDs now due to this change?
faq.a: There's no immediate need to move your FDs solely based on this rule. The impact on retail FD rates is indirect. However, it's always prudent to compare rates across banks regularly to ensure you are getting competitive returns.

faq.q: How can I find the best FD rates?
faq.a: You can compare FD rates on bank websites, financial news portals, or by consulting financial advisors. Look for banks offering competitive rates for your desired tenure, keeping in mind your liquidity needs.

faq.q: Will all banks offer differential rates on bulk deposits?
faq.a: Banks now *have the option* to offer differential rates on bulk deposits based on their liquidity risk. It is up to each individual bank to decide whether and how to implement this flexibility.

RBI policy changes are generally made with a long-term view to enhance financial stability and efficiency. While policies can be reviewed and refined, the underlying principle of allowing banks more flexibility in liquidity management is likely to persist.
